editorial:
You are dropped right back into the middle of a galaxy at war, where the Resistance is on the run and the First Order is closing in fast. Rey has found Luke Skywalker on a lonely island, hoping he will train her, but he is broken and unsure about teaching anyone. Meanwhile, Finn and Poe are trying to keep the fleet alive while Kylo Ren wrestles with his own dark path. The whole movie feels bigger and riskier than the last one, with real stakes and surprises around every corner.

The action is huge and the visuals are stunning, especially the space battles and the red salt planet showdown. Mark Hamill gives a powerful, emotional performance as an older, conflicted Luke, and Daisy Ridley keeps Rey grounded and relatable. Some fans did not love the bold story choices, and a few side plots slow things down, but the movie still delivers thrills and heart. If you enjoy big sci-fi adventures with twists, this is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: Rey and Kylo Ren team up briefly to fight Snoke's guards, but Kylo then turns on Rey and claims the First Order for himself. Luke appears on the salt planet to face Kylo, but it is actually a Force projection, buying time for the Resistance to escape. Luke peacefully fades away, becoming one with the Force. Rey lifts the rocks to free the trapped survivors, and the small group escapes aboard the Millennium Falcon, keeping hope alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves big space adventures and bold twists.
